reasons.reason: R1 and R2 are split into four separate rubric items (rb1, rb2 for approved Operations/Supplies; rb3, rb4 for actual Operations/Supplies) that mirror the same requirement without distinct verification targets; this double-counts the underlying reporting criteria across items that test the same declared requirement_id, inflating their effective weight. Additionally, R3's verification spec reads the difference_usd column but the unit_evidence_id points to the actual row evidence rather than a unit-declaring evidence for the difference, and the requirement description in the task says the difference is 'reported per category' in both d1 and d2 while the numeric spec only checks the CSV, leaving the markdown interpretation effectively untested for the sign/value of the difference beyond the single semantic item. These are alignment/weighting defects rather than fatal gaps, but they prevent full alignment with the declared requirement structure.

Two defects. First, rb8 (input_final_integrity) and rb9 (requires_execution_trace) both test R5 with weights 10 and 5; the execution-trace item is the sound test for the process claim, while the final-integrity hash is described in the review instruction as unable to prove the absence of intermediate writes, so splitting R5 across two items double-counts the same constraint and awards weight to a weaker check. Second, rb10 (R6, semantic) and rb7 (R4, semantic) overlap heavily: rb7's conflict policy already fails any report that asserts authority to transfer funds or directs an unapproved transfer, and rb10 tests the same policy constraint again with an additional weight, double-counting the policy constraint. The numeric formula specs themselves are otherwise correct (operands, signs, zero tolerances, USD unit traceable to source rows).

The requirement itself is explicit and policy-supported, but it is tested by two overlapping rubric items (rb8 final-integrity hash at weight 10 and rb9 execution-trace at weight 5). The review instruction states that final hashes cannot claim to test trace-only constraints; therefore the 10-weight hash item is an unsound substitute for the process claim, and R5 is double-counted. The process claim should be carried by the trace item alone.

The requirement is explicit and policy-supported, but its scored item rb10 duplicates the transfer-authority policy constraint already covered inside R4's semantic item rb7, which explicitly fails any report that asserts authority to transfer funds or directs an unapproved transfer. This double-counts the same policy constraint with an additional weight, so the scored coverage is not independent.

Unsound as a scored check for a trace-only constraint. input_final_integrity compares final hashes only and cannot demonstrate that no write, edit, rename or deletion occurred during execution; the review instruction explicitly forbids claiming trace-only constraints via final hashes. It also duplicates rb9 on the same requirement_id R5 and assigns it the larger weight (10 vs 5), double-counting the constraint.

The semantic item is grounded in the policy evidence and its full_credit/common_errors are concrete, but it duplicates the same transfer-authority constraint already enforced by rb7's conflict_policy, which fails any report asserting authority to transfer funds or directing an unapproved transfer. Scoring both items double-counts the policy constraint.
